questions.question_text: Which international organization is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland?
questions.explanation: The WTO is headquartered in Geneva, whereas the UN is in New York, and IMF/World Bank are in Washington D.C.

questions.question_text: What is the primary objective of the 'Circular Economy' model?
options: Reducing waste and extending product lifecycles
questions.explanation: The circular economy is a model of production and consumption which involves sharing, leasing, reusing, repairing, refurbishing, and recycling existing materials and products as long as possible.

questions.question_text: Which planet is known as the 'Red Planet'?
questions.explanation: Mars is referred to as the Red Planet due to iron oxide on its surface.

questions.question_text: Who is the author of 'The Wealth of Nations'?
questions.explanation: Adam Smith is considered the father of economics and wrote this seminal work in 1776.

questions.question_text: What is the primary currency of Japan?
questions.explanation: The Yen is the official currency of Japan.

questions.question_text: Which gas is most abundant in the Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen makes up approximately 78% of the Earth's atmosphere.

questions.question_text: What is the capital of Canada?
questions.explanation: Ottawa is the capital city of Canada.

questions.question_text: The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in which city?
questions.explanation: While other Nobel prizes are awarded in Stockholm, the Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo, Norway.

questions.question_text: What does 'GDP' stand for in economics?
questions.explanation: GDP is the total market value of all finished goods and services produced within a country's borders.

questions.question_text: Who is known as the founder of Microsoft?
What is the largest ocean in the world?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest of Earth's oceanic divisions.

questions.question_text: Which organization focuses on international monetary cooperation?
questions.explanation: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) works to foster global monetary cooperation and financial stability.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a renewable energy source?
questions.explanation: Geothermal energy is derived from the heat of the Earth and is considered renewable.

questions.question_text: Which international body oversees global trade rules?
questions.explanation: The World Trade Organization (WTO) deals with the global rules of trade between nations.
